cards.f: Relative charges of proton, neutron, electron
Proton number Z and nucleon number A
cards.b: Z = number of protons; A = number of protons + neutrons. Neutrons = A − Z.
Atoms of the same element (same protons) with different numbers of neutrons.
Radon gas in the air, rocks and buildings, food and drink, cosmic rays.

cards.f: Nature of α, β and γ
cards.b: α: helium nucleus (2 protons, 2 neutrons). β: fast electron from the nucleus. γ: electromagnetic radiation.

cards.f: Ionising power and penetration of α, β, γ
cards.b: α: most ionising, stopped by paper/few cm of air. β: medium, stopped by few mm of aluminium. γ: least ionising, reduced by thick lead/concrete.
Spontaneous: not affected by temperature or chemical reactions. Random: can't predict which nucleus decays or when.
A decreases by 4 and Z decreases by 2; the nucleus becomes a different element.
A neutron changes into a proton and an electron (emitted). A unchanged, Z increases by 1.
The time taken for half the nuclei of that isotope in any sample to decay.

cards.f: Why use γ to sterilise equipment?
cards.b: It penetrates packaging and kills bacteria.

cards.f: Why is α used in smoke alarms?
cards.b: α ionises air between plates giving a small current; smoke absorbs α, the current drops and the alarm sounds.
Short time, large distance (tongs), shielding (lead-lined containers).

cards.f: Order of the planets from the Sun
cards.b: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
Distance light travels in space in one year (about 9.5 × 10¹⁵ m). A unit of distance, not time.

The Sun's energy comes from nuclear ___ of hydrogen into helium.
Light takes 500 s to reach Earth from the Sun. At 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s the distance is 1.5 × 10___ m.
The planet between Mars and Saturn is ___ .

short.q: A radioactive source has a count rate of 640 counts/min. Its half-life is 3.0 h. Calculate the count rate after 12 h.
Complete the decay equation for uranium-238 (Z = 92) emitting an α-particle: ²³⁸₉₂U → ?Th + ⁴₂He. State the nucleon and proton numbers of thorium.
short.model: Thorium has nucleon number 234 and proton number 90 (²³⁴₉₀Th), since 238 − 4 = 234 and 92 − 2 = 90.

short.q: Explain why a gamma source is used to sterilise surgical instruments sealed in plastic packaging.
short.model: Gamma radiation penetrates the packaging and kills bacteria on the instruments, so they are sterilised without opening.

short.q: Describe the life cycle of a star with about the mass of the Sun.
short.model: A cloud of gas and dust collapses under gravity to a protostar, then a stable star (hydrogen fusion). It becomes a red giant, then a white dwarf with a planetary nebula.
points: cloud of gas and dust → protostar

short.q: Mars orbits the Sun at radius 2.3 × 10¹¹ m with period 5.9 × 10⁷ s. Calculate its orbital speed.
